text:
sarah_sales: Quick check — AcmeCorp is asking for committed capacity for a POC. They expect a 95th p99 latency SLA and ~1.8k QPS bursty traffic (chat + embed mix). Can we confirm recommended reserved GPU count and an autoscale fallback plan?
omar_sre: Do we have the traffic mix breakdown? embeddings vs chat, average seq len, concurrency per session?
lina_eng: From the questionnaire: ~60% chat (avg 150 tokens), 40% embeddings (avg 512 dims), peak concurrency ~1200 concurrent in short spikes, steady-state ~300 qps. Model pinned to redwood/llm-7b-quantized.
mike_solution: Pricing concern from Acme: they want predictability. They asked for an estimate of reserved vGPU-hours vs burst credit billing. Also worried about preheat costs for KV warmup.
sarah_sales: Exactly. They asked for a monthly committed slot quote + a fallback burst policy. They want to avoid unexpected overage charges during peak campaigns.
omar_sre: Proposed approach: reserve enough GPUs to cover 95% of expected sustained load (steady-state 300 qps). Use reserved pool + autoscale for spikes. Autoscale should have a fast scale-up (1–2min) and graceful scale-down (10–15min) to avoid thrashing.
lina_eng: Quick math: redwood/llm-7b-quantized on A100-80GB: ~40 qps per GPU for chat at 150 tokens, embeddings ~1200 embeddings/s per GPU depending on batch. Mixed workload effective throughput ~= 60 qps/GPU. For steady 300 qps -> 5 GPUs reserved. For peak 1800 qps -> 30 GPUs total, so 25 GPUs as burst capacity.
mike_solution: Can we structure pricing as: 5 reserved GPUs at X/mo + burst credits for up to 25 extra GPUs billed at burst rate Y/hr? Also include a preheat window cost estimate for KV warming.
omar_sre: Yeah. Also recommend we add model-variant fallback: when reserved pool saturated, route to a lower-cost quantized variant (llm-7b-q4f16) with a quality disclaimer. That keeps latency SLOs while reducing overage cost.
sarah_sales: Acme is sensitive to output quality. They want automatic fallbacks but only if quality drop is within acceptable delta. Can we attach a canary ratio?
lina_eng: Suggest canary: 10% traffic to fallback variant during spikes, monitor eval metric (ROUGE/embedding cosine) and escalate if drop > 2%. Rollback threshold configurable.
omar_sre: Operationally we should codify autoscale and routing in the reserved deployment config. Example config snippet: 
```
reserved_capacity:
  reserved_nodes: 5
  min_nodes: 5
  max_nodes: 30
  scale_up: {threshold_qps: 350, cooldown: 60}
  scale_down: {threshold_qps: 200, cooldown: 600}
fallbacks:
  - variant: llm-7b-q4f16
    canary_pct: 10
    max_pct_on_surge: 50
```

mike_solution: Perfect — can you also add preheat plan? They run multi-hour marketing blasts and want KV warmup before the window. We should estimate tokens to warm up and cost.
lina_eng: KV warm is cheap but time-consuming. If we preheat the KV cache for their common prefixes: estimate ~200M tokens warm -> ~3 GPU-hours for warm per region. Add 4–6 hours of reserved preheat to be safe.
omar_sre: Suggest offering a preheat add-on: one-time preheat reservation of 6 GPU-hours during campaign start for $Z. Also include a runbook step to monitor tail latency and KV hit rate.
sarah_sales: Security note: Acme's legal wants KMS integration and audit logs for private deployment. Can we confirm Private (VPC) option?
mike_solution: Yes — Private supports customer KMS and audit logging. That adds an enterprise SKU and on-prem licensing/fee. Call it out in the proposal.
omar_sre: Also checklist items for onboarding: IP allowlist, KMS key ARN, SOC2 attestation, and a quarterly key rotation window.
sarah_sales: OK. For the sales quote: base reserved 5 GPUs, burst credit for up to 25 GPUs, optional preheat 6 GPU-hrs, private deployment flag for KMS/audit. Can someone draft numbers to share with Acme?
lina_eng: I can draft an engineering sizing doc with throughput assumptions and expected tail latency at each scale point. Will include cost delta for fallback variant.
omar_sre: I'll add an ops section with autoscale knobs, preheat runbook, and SLA caveats.
mike_solution: I'll translate to pricing language and include examples of monthly cost under typical vs campaign scenarios.
sarah_sales: Thanks team. Can we sync with Acme on Wed 11am PT? I'll schedule. @ops-bot: create follow-up ticket for preheat runbook and pricing appendix.
ops-bot: Created ticket #PR-8741: "AcmeCorp — preheat runbook + pricing appendix" assigned to lina_eng, omar_sre, due 2026-03-30. :white_check_mark:
sarah_sales: Great. One more ask from Acme: What happens if a zone goes down mid-campaign? Do we have cross-AZ fallback?
omar_sre: We recommend AZ spread for reserved nodes (minimum 3 AZs for 5 GPUs). Add region fallback policy to route traffic to another region with replicated cache; note replication increases preheat cost.
lina_eng: I'll add a short paragraph describing replication tradeoffs (latency vs cost) — estimate 2x preheat if we replicate KV across regions.
msg_end: "Thanks all — will update the doc and loop in Legal for KMS wording."
